en: whoops; oh my goodness; oh my gosh

examples.en: Oh my goodness, I left my wallet at home!
Whoops, I dropped the cup and it broke!
Oh my gosh, it's already past our meeting time!
Oh my goodness, the child fell down the stairs!

examples.ko: 아이고머니나, 비가 오는데 빨래를 널어 놓았어요!
examples.en: Oh my gosh, I hung the laundry out and now it's raining!

examples.ko: 아이고머니나, 이렇게 큰 선물을 주셔서 정말 고마워요!
examples.en: Oh my goodness, thank you so much for such a big gift!

explain: 깜짝 놀라거나 당황했을 때 나오는 말로, '아이고'나 '어머나'보다 조금 더 과장된 느낌이에요. 친한 사이에서 말하거나 드라마 대사에서 자주 들을 수 있어요. 격식을 차리는 자리나 글에서는 잘 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: This is what people say when they are startled or flustered, and it feels a bit more exaggerated than '아이고' or '어머나'. You will hear it among close people and in TV dramas. It is not used in formal situations or in writing.

examples.en: Today I tried putting on brown eye shadow.
This eye shadow sparkles nicely around the eyes.
My eye shadow smeared and came off because of sweat.
I got sparkly eye shadow as a gift from a friend.

examples.ko: 아이섀도 색깔을 고르는 게 너무 어려워요.
examples.en: Choosing an eye shadow color is so hard.
Which eye shadow color suits me?

explain: 눈 화장에 쓰는 화장품이고, 외래어 표기법에 따라 '아이쉐도'가 아니라 '아이섀도'라고 써요. 화장품 가게에서는 '아이라이너', '마스카라'와 함께 자주 나와요. 바르다, 칠하다, 하다와 같이 써요.
explain_en: This is makeup for the eyelids, and the standard spelling is '아이섀도', not '아이쉐도'. It often appears together with '아이라이너' (eyeliner) and '마스카라' (mascara) at cosmetics shops. It goes with verbs like 바르다, 칠하다 and 하다.

examples.ko: 낚시 갈 때 아이스박스에 음료수를 가득 넣었어요.
examples.en: When we went fishing, I filled the cooler with drinks.

examples.ko: 아이스박스 안에 얼음이 아직 남아 있어요.
examples.en: There is still some ice left in the cooler.
We brought a big cooler to the campsite.
I bought fish and brought it back in a cooler.

examples.ko: 이 아이스박스는 무거워서 혼자 들기 힘들어요.
examples.en: This cooler is heavy, so it's hard to lift alone.

examples.ko: 아이스박스가 없으면 고기가 상할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Without a cooler, the meat could spoil.

explain: 한국어에서는 얼음을 넣어 음식과 음료를 차갑게 들고 다니는 상자만 가리켜요. 집에서 쓰는 냉장고는 '냉장고'라고 해요. 캠핑, 낚시, 소풍 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: In Korean this only means the portable box you fill with ice to keep food and drinks cold. The fridge at home is just '냉장고'. It often comes up when talking about camping, fishing and picnics.

examples.en: Jeez, you didn't bring your keys again?
Jeez, don't tease me like that.

examples.ko: 아이참, 왜 이렇게 말을 안 들어요?
examples.en: Jeez, why won't you listen?
Jeez, the picnic got canceled because of the rain.
Jeez, please stop talking about that now.
Jeez, I was about to say it first.

explain: 조금 답답하거나 못마땅할 때, 또는 쑥스러울 때 가볍게 내는 소리예요. 화를 내기보다 투정하거나 애교 섞인 느낌이 있어서 가까운 사이에서 많이 써요. 윗사람에게 크게 말하면 버릇없게 들릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is a light exclamation for mild annoyance, frustration or embarrassment. It sounds more like a playful complaint than real anger, so it is used mostly between close people. Saying it loudly to a superior can sound rude.

examples.en: I still haven't heard from that person.

examples.ko: 아직껏 한국 음식을 먹어 본 적이 없어요.
examples.en: I have never tried Korean food until now.
You still haven't finished your homework?
I still can't forget that.
The rain still hasn't stopped.
My younger sibling is still sleeping.

explain: '아직'을 강하게 말하는 느낌이고, 보통 '아직도 안 했다'처럼 기대한 일이 지금까지 안 된 상황에 많이 써요. 비슷한 말로 '여태껏'이 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '아직'이나 '아직도'를 더 많이 쓰고, '아직껏'은 조금 강조하거나 글에서 써요.
explain_en: It is a stronger version of '아직' and is often used when something expected still hasn't happened. A similar word is '여태껏'. In everyday talk people usually say just '아직' or '아직도', and '아직껏' sounds more emphatic or written.

examples.en: This bridge was built in an arch shape.

examples.ko: 아치형 문을 지나면 작은 정원이 나와요.
examples.en: Past the arched gate, there is a small garden.

examples.ko: 아치형 창문이 있는 카페가 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: The cafe with arched windows is very popular.
They decorated the entrance nicely in an arch shape.

examples.ko: 아치형 천장이 높아서 공간이 넓어 보여요.
examples.en: The arched ceiling is high, so the space looks wide.

examples.ko: 사진 찍기 좋은 아치형 터널이 있어요.
examples.en: There is an arched tunnel that is great for taking photos.

explain: 위쪽은 둥글게 굽고 아래쪽은 뚫린 모양을 말해서 다리, 문, 창문, 천장에 자주 써요. 그냥 '둥근 모양'과 달리 문이나 통로처럼 아래가 열려 있는 모양을 떠올리면 돼요. 뒤에 '으로'나 다른 명사가 붙는 일이 많아요.
explain_en: It describes a shape that curves at the top and is open at the bottom, so it is often used for bridges, gates, windows and ceilings. Unlike a plain '둥근 모양' (round shape), picture something with an opening like a doorway or passage. It is often followed by '으로' or another noun.

examples.en: Maybe because it was still the forenoon, there were no customers in the shop.
The weather was clear in the morning, but it turned cloudy in the afternoon.
I did nothing but clean the whole morning.

examples.ko: 내일 아침나절에 잠깐 만날 수 있어요?
examples.en: Can we meet briefly tomorrow morning?
The morning sunlight comes warmly into the living room.
I have to finish the work by late morning.

explain: 아침부터 점심 전까지 어느 정도 이어지는 시간을 말해서 '아침 한 시점'보다 길게 느껴져요. 저녁 무렵은 '저녁나절'이라고 해요. '오전'보다 부드럽고 이야기 같은 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It covers a stretch of time from morning until before noon, so it feels longer than a single point in the morning. The evening counterpart is '저녁나절'. It sounds softer and more story-like than '오전'.

examples.en: My mother set out a breakfast table for me.
Kimchi stew and rolled omelet were on the breakfast table.
I cleared the breakfast table and did the dishes.
The family sits around the breakfast table and talks.
The breakfast spread was so generous that I was surprised.
I was served a lovingly prepared breakfast at my grandmother's house.

explain: '아침밥'이나 '아침 식사'보다 상 위에 음식이 차려진 모습이 떠오르는 말이에요. '아침상을 차리다', '아침상을 치우다', '아침상을 받다'처럼 써요. 같은 방식으로 '점심상', '저녁상'도 말할 수 있어요.
explain_en: Compared with '아침밥' or '아침 식사', this word makes you picture the table with the food laid out on it. It is used in phrases like '아침상을 차리다' (set the table), '치우다' (clear) and '받다' (be served). In the same way you can say '점심상' and '저녁상'.

en: shut one's teeth; set one's teeth

examples.ko: 그 사람을 잊겠다고 다짐하며 이를 악물었어요.
examples.en: I clenched my teeth, resolving to forget that person.
Even though it hurt, I gritted my teeth and ran to the end.
I keep clenching my teeth, so my jaw hurts.

examples.ko: 눈물이 나는 걸 이를 악물고 참았어요.
examples.en: I held back my tears by gritting my teeth.
This time I will study with all my determination.
Don't clench your teeth; relax.

explain: 거의 '이를 악물다', '어금니를 악물다'처럼 이와 함께 써요. 정말 이를 꽉 무는 동작도 되고, 힘든 일을 참거나 굳게 결심하는 모습을 말할 때도 많이 써요. '악물고'로 이어서 뒤에 오는 동작을 꾸미는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 아프거나 마음이 힘들어도 참고 해내려는 의지가 강할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone endures pain or hardship with strong determination to get through it.

explain_en: It is almost always used with 이 (teeth), as in '이를 악물다' or '어금니를 악물다'. It can mean really clenching your teeth, but it is also often used for enduring something hard or making a firm resolve. The form '악물고' is often used to describe the action that follows.

examples.ko: 악조건 속에서도 선수들은 끝까지 최선을 다했어요.
examples.en: Even under bad conditions, the players did their best to the end.
We overcame the bad conditions of rain and wind.
Bad conditions piled up, and the construction was delayed a lot.
It is dangerous to drive in conditions like these.
Despite the bad conditions, we finished the match safely.
We canceled the hike because of several unfavorable conditions.

explain: 날씨, 환경, 형편이 좋지 않아 일하기 힘든 상황을 말해요. 반대말은 '호조건'이고, 일상에서는 '좋은 조건'이라고도 많이 말해요. '악조건 속에서', '악조건을 이기다', '악조건을 극복하다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: It describes poor circumstances, such as weather, environment or situation, that make things hard. The opposite is '호조건', and in daily talk people also just say '좋은 조건'. Common patterns are '악조건 속에서', '악조건을 이기다' and '악조건을 극복하다'.

examples.ko: 제가 악필이라서 메모를 남에게 못 보여 줘요.
examples.en: My handwriting is bad, so I can't show my notes to others.
I had a hard time reading my friend's messy handwriting.
I started practicing writing to fix my bad handwriting.

examples.ko: 악필이라서 제 글씨를 저도 못 읽어요.
examples.en: My handwriting is so bad that even I can't read it.

examples.ko: 손으로 쓸 일이 줄어서 악필이 더 심해졌어요.
examples.en: I write by hand less now, so my handwriting got even worse.
Even bad handwriting can get prettier with effort.

explain: 글씨를 알아보기 힘들게 쓰는 것을 말하고, 자기 글씨를 두고 '저 악필이에요'라고 웃으며 말하는 일이 많아요. 반대로 글씨를 잘 쓰면 '달필'이라고 하고, 아주 잘 쓰는 사람은 '명필'이라고 해요. '글씨를 못 쓰다'는 더 평범한 표현이에요.
explain_en: It means writing so messily that it is hard to read, and people often joke about their own handwriting with '저 악필이에요'. The opposite is '달필' for good handwriting, and '명필' for someone who writes exceptionally well. '글씨를 못 쓰다' is a plainer way to say it.

examples.en: I made a bouquet by adding baby's breath to the roses.

examples.ko: 안개꽃은 작고 하얀 꽃이 많이 피어요.
examples.en: Baby's breath blooms with many small white flowers.
I put a bunch of baby's breath in a vase.

examples.ko: 안개꽃이 있으니 꽃다발이 더 풍성해 보여요.
examples.en: With the baby's breath, the bouquet looks fuller.
I tried decorating my room with baby's breath.
I dry baby's breath and use it as decoration.

explain: 장미 같은 큰 꽃 사이에 채워 넣는 꽃으로 꽃다발이나 꽃꽂이에서 자주 보여요. 작은 꽃이 구름이나 안개처럼 퍼져 보이는 모습이 특징이에요. 말려서 드라이플라워로 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It is a flower often tucked between bigger flowers like roses in bouquets and arrangements. Its small blooms spread out like a cloud or mist. People also dry it and use it as a dried flower.

examples.en: I put an armchair in the living room.
I sat in an armchair and read a book.
This armchair is really comfortable.
The armchair was so soft that I fell asleep.
My father sits in the armchair and watches the news.
I went to a furniture store to buy an armchair.

explain: 등받이와 팔걸이가 있고 푹신해서 편하게 앉는 의자를 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '편한 의자'나 '소파'라고 말하는 경우도 많아요. 가구점 설명이나 글에서 더 자주 보이는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is a soft chair with a back and armrests that you can relax in. In daily conversation people often say '편한 의자' or '소파' instead. The word shows up more in furniture descriptions and writing.

examples.en: My shoulders hurt, so I bought a massager.
I held the massager to my neck and turned it on.
This massager is quiet.
I gave my parents a massager as a gift.
It feels refreshing to loosen up my calves with a massager.
The massager broke, so I had it repaired.

explain: 몸을 주물러 주는 기계를 말하고, 의자처럼 앉아서 쓰는 큰 제품은 '안마의자'라고 해요. 같은 뜻으로 '마사지기'라고도 많이 말해요. 어깨, 목, 종아리 등 쓰는 부위를 앞에 붙여 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It means a machine that kneads and massages your body, and the big chair-type product is called '안마의자'. People also commonly say '마사지기' for the same thing. You can add the body part in front, such as shoulders, neck or calves.

examples.en: The masseur carefully loosened my shoulders.
I got a back massage from a masseur.
I am studying to get a massage therapist license.
This masseur has really strong hands.
There is a well-known masseur in our neighborhood.

examples.ko: 안마사께 조금 더 세게 해 달라고 부탁했어요.
examples.en: I asked the masseur to press a little harder.

explain: 안마를 직업으로 하는 사람을 말해요. 일상에서는 '마사지'라는 말도 많이 써서, 마사지를 해 주는 사람을 '마사지사'라고도 해요. 누군가의 몸을 직접 주물러 주는 사람이라서 '안마기'와는 달리 사람을 가리켜요.
explain_en: It refers to a person who works as a masseur. In daily life people also use the word '마사지', so someone who gives massages may be called a '마사지사'. Unlike '안마기', which is a machine, this word refers to a person.

examples.en: Be sure to keep a safe distance from the car ahead.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에는 안전거리를 더 길게 두어야 해요.
examples.en: On rainy days, you should leave a longer safe distance.

examples.ko: 안전거리를 확보하지 않으면 사고가 날 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you don't keep a safe distance, an accident can happen.
The distance was so short that I got a scare.

examples.ko: 운전 학원에서 안전거리 유지하는 법을 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned how to keep a safe distance at driving school.

examples.ko: 사람들 사이에 안전거리를 두고 서 주세요.
examples.en: Please stand with some safe distance between people.

explain: 운전할 때 앞차와 부딪히지 않도록 띄워야 하는 거리를 가장 먼저 떠올려요. '확보하다', '유지하다', '지키다'와 자주 같이 써요. 사람들 사이에 필요한 거리를 말할 때도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It most often brings to mind the distance you must leave from the car ahead so you don't collide. It pairs with verbs like '확보하다', '유지하다' and '지키다'. It can also refer to the space needed between people.

examples.ko: 소비자 피해를 막으려면 개인의 주의보다 제도적 안전망이 먼저예요.
examples.en: To prevent consumer harm, an institutional safety net comes before individual caution.

examples.ko: 건설 현장에는 추락을 막는 안전망이 설치돼 있어요.
examples.en: Construction sites have safety nets installed to prevent falls.

examples.ko: 사회 안전망이 약하면 어려운 사람이 더 힘들어져요.
examples.en: If the social safety net is weak, people in need suffer even more.

examples.ko: 실직했을 때 도움을 받을 안전망이 필요해요.
examples.en: We need a safety net to rely on when we lose a job.
They installed a safety net under the ceiling of the concert hall.
Thanks to the safety net, I avoided a serious injury.

explain: 떨어지는 사람이나 물건을 받아 주는 그물이라는 실제 뜻과, 어려운 사람을 지키는 제도라는 비유로 모두 써요. 뉴스에서는 '사회 안전망', '복지 안전망'처럼 자주 나와요. '안전망을 갖추다', '안전망을 확충하다'와 같이 쓰는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is used both for a real net that catches people or objects falling, and figuratively for systems that protect people in hardship. In the news you often see '사회 안전망' (social safety net) and '복지 안전망'. Typical phrases are '안전망을 갖추다' and '안전망을 확충하다'.

examples.en: I was restless while waiting for the exam results.
My parents are on edge because the child is late.
Why are you so fidgety?
I was so restless before the interview that I only drank water.

examples.ko: 그는 안절부절못하는 모습으로 방 안을 서성였어요.
examples.en: He paced around the room looking anxious and restless.
I'm anxious in case my secret gets found out.

explain: 불안하거나 초조해서 가만히 있지 못하고 서성이는 모습을 말해요. 표준어는 '안절부절못하다'이고 한 단어로 붙여 써요. '안절부절못하는 모습'처럼 뒤에서 꾸미는 말로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It describes being so anxious or nervous that you cannot stay still and keep pacing or fidgeting. The standard form is '안절부절못하다', written as one word. It is also commonly used before a noun, as in '안절부절못하는 모습'.

examples.en: I entered the stable stage of pregnancy, and my morning sickness lessened.
The exchange rate has entered a stable period, so I worry less.
My child has passed puberty and entered a calmer phase.

examples.ko: 회사가 안정기를 맞아 직원을 더 뽑고 있어요.
examples.en: The company has reached a stable phase and is hiring more staff.
During the stable period, it's fine to increase exercise little by little.

examples.ko: 안정기가 올 때까지 시간이 좀 더 걸릴 것 같아요.
examples.en: It looks like it will take a bit longer until things become stable.

explain: 불안하고 흔들리던 시기가 지나고 차분해진 시기를 말해요. 임신 이야기에서 '안정기'가 자주 나와요. 형광등에 쓰는 부품 이름도 '안정기'라서 문맥을 보고 구별해야 해요.
explain_en: It refers to a calm period after an unsettled time. It comes up a lot in talk about pregnancy. A part used in fluorescent lamps is also called '안정기', so you need to tell them apart from context.

examples.en: Prices are showing a stable trend.
Housing prices have turned stable.
The exchange rate has entered a stable trend.
The market has regained stability this year.
The stable trend continued, so running a shop became easier.
They say government measures are needed to keep things stable.

explain: 가격이나 경기가 크게 오르내리지 않고 차분해지는 흐름을 말하는 뉴스 용어예요. '-세'는 '상승세', '하락세'처럼 흐름을 나타내서 반대로는 '불안정'하거나 '급등세'처럼 말해요. '안정세를 보이다', '안정세를 찾다', '안정세에 접어들다'와 함께 써요.
explain_en: This is a news term for a trend in which prices or the economy calm down instead of swinging a lot. The suffix '-세' marks a trend, as in '상승세' (rising trend) and '하락세' (falling trend). It goes with '안정세를 보이다', '안정세를 찾다' and '안정세에 접어들다'.

examples.en: The government announced measures to stabilize prices.
It takes time for the exchange rate to stabilize.

examples.ko: 서비스 안정화 작업 때문에 앱이 잠시 멈춰요.
examples.en: The app stops for a while because of stabilization work on the service.

examples.ko: 신제품 출시 후 서비스 안정화에 힘쓰고 있어요.
examples.en: After the new product launch, we are working hard on stabilizing the service.

examples.ko: 가격 안정화를 위해 수입을 늘리기로 했어요.
examples.en: They decided to increase imports to stabilize prices.

examples.ko: 마음의 안정화에는 규칙적인 생활이 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: A regular routine helps your mind settle down.

explain: 흔들리던 것이 안정되는 과정을 말하고, 뉴스나 회사에서 '물가 안정화', '시스템 안정화'처럼 자주 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '안정되다'나 '자리를 잡다'라고 말하는 경우가 더 많아요. 뒤에 '대책', '작업', '단계'가 붙는 일이 많아요.
explain_en: It refers to the process of something unsteady becoming stable, and is common in news and workplaces, as in '물가 안정화' and '시스템 안정화'. In everyday talk people more often say '안정되다' or '자리를 잡다'. It is often followed by nouns like '대책', '작업' and '단계'.

examples.en: The lady of the house brought out warm tea for the guests.

examples.ko: 이 집 안주인이 음식 솜씨가 정말 좋아요.
examples.en: The lady of this house is a really good cook.
I said goodbye to the lady of the house and left.

examples.ko: 한옥 안주인이 방을 정성껏 정리해 주었어요.
examples.en: The hostess of the hanok carefully tidied up the room for us.

examples.ko: 새로 온 안주인은 집안일을 잘 챙겨요.
examples.en: The new lady of the house takes good care of the household.

examples.ko: 안주인이 안 계셔서 다음에 다시 올게요.
examples.en: The lady of the house isn't here, so I'll come again next time.

explain: 집안일을 맡아 하는 집의 여주인을 말하고, 반대말은 '바깥주인'이에요. 가게나 식당 이야기에서는 보통 '사장님'이라고 불러요. 윗사람에 대해 말할 때는 '안주인께서'처럼 높여 말해요.
explain_en: It means the woman who runs the household, and the opposite is '바깥주인'. For shops and restaurants people usually say '사장님' instead. When talking about someone senior, you honor it like '안주인께서'.

examples.ko: 어린이집 알림장에는 오늘 아이가 친구와 블록 놀이를 했다고 적혀 있어요.
examples.en: The daycare notebook says my child played with blocks with a friend today.
The teacher wrote the things to bring in the notice notebook.
Be sure to show the notice notebook to your parents.
Please check today's notice notebook and sign it.
I forgot to write the homework in my notice notebook.
I looked at my child's notebook, and it says there is a field trip tomorrow.

explain: 어린이집, 유치원, 초등학교에서 선생님이 부모님께 전하는 소식이나 숙제, 준비물을 적는 공책이에요. '알림장을 쓰다', '알림장을 확인하다'처럼 써요. 요즘은 앱으로 보내는 경우도 있어서 '알림장 앱'이라는 말도 써요.
explain_en: It is the notebook used at daycare, kindergarten and elementary school for teachers to write news, homework and things to bring for parents. It goes with '알림장을 쓰다' and '알림장을 확인하다'. Nowadays some schools send it through an app, so you also hear '알림장 앱'.

examples.en: I picked up a pocketful of chestnuts on the mountain.
In autumn, chestnuts drop with a thud.
I roasted chestnuts and shared them with my family.
Not many chestnuts grew this year.
My grandmother peeled chestnuts for me.
The chestnuts are big and sweet, so they're delicious.

explain: 밤송이 속에서 빠져나온 굵은 밤톨을 말해요. 구운 밤은 '군밤'이라고 해서 따로 불러요. 밤송이에서 나온 밤을 줍는 '밤 줍기'는 가을 체험으로도 인기가 있어요.

phrases.en: to give someone a light knock on the head
phrases.nuance_ko: 주먹으로 머리를 가볍게 콩 때리는 장난스러운 행동이에요. 가족이나 친구 사이에서 쓰고 크게 다치게 하는 뜻은 아니에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means playfully knocking someone on the head with a fist. It is used among family and friends and does not mean hurting someone badly.
phrases.en_equiv: give someone a knuckle knock on the head

explain_en: It refers to a plump chestnut that has come out of its spiky burr. Roasted chestnuts have their own name, '군밤'. Picking up chestnuts in autumn is also a popular seasonal activity.

examples.en: After working out, I got a bulge of muscle in my arm.

examples.ko: 알통을 보여 달라고 했더니 팔에 힘을 줬어요.
examples.en: When I asked him to show his muscles, he flexed his arm.

examples.ko: 동생이 알통 자랑을 해서 웃음이 났어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling bragged about his muscles, and it made me laugh.

examples.ko: 알통이 불끈 솟은 팔이 정말 멋있어요.
examples.en: An arm with bulging muscles looks really cool.
If you do push-ups every day, your arm muscles get bigger.
The child lifts a dumbbell, saying he wants to build up his arm muscles.

explain: 팔에 힘을 줄 때 볼록하게 솟는 근육을 말하고, '근육'보다 귀엽고 친근한 느낌이에요. 주로 '알통이 생기다', '알통을 만들다', '알통을 보여 주다'처럼 써요. 아이들이 팔에 힘을 주며 자랑할 때도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It means the muscle that bulges when you flex your arm, and it sounds cuter and friendlier than '근육'. It is typically used as '알통이 생기다', '알통을 만들다' and '알통을 보여 주다'. Kids often use it when showing off by flexing their arms.

examples.en: The hen lays eggs every morning.

examples.ko: 암탉 한 마리가 병아리들을 데리고 다녀요.
examples.en: A hen is walking around with her chicks.
They raise hens at my grandmother's house in the countryside.
I learned how to tell hens and roosters apart.
A hen is pecking at feed in the yard.

examples.ko: 이 암탉은 알을 품고 있어서 예민해요.
examples.en: This hen is sitting on her eggs, so she is touchy.

explain: 암컷 닭을 말하고, 수컷은 '수탉'이라고 해요. '탉'의 받침 ㄺ이 [ㄱ]으로 소리 나서 [암탁], [수탁]으로 읽어요. '닭'은 암수를 구별하지 않을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It means a female chicken, and the male is '수탉'. The final cluster ㄺ in '탉' sounds like ㄱ, so they are pronounced [암탁] and [수탁]. '닭' is the general word when you don't distinguish sex.

examples.en: Scalped tickets for the popular concert were posted online.

examples.ko: 암표를 샀다가 사기를 당할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you buy a scalped ticket, you can get scammed.

examples.ko: 암표 거래는 문제가 돼서 단속하고 있어요.
examples.en: Ticket scalping is a problem, so it is being cracked down on.

examples.ko: 암표 값이 원래 가격보다 몇 배나 비싸요.
examples.en: The scalped price is several times the original price.

examples.ko: 경기장 앞에서 암표를 파는 사람을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw someone selling scalped tickets in front of the stadium.

examples.ko: 암표 때문에 정작 팬들은 표를 구하기 어려워요.
examples.en: Because of scalpers, real fans have a hard time getting tickets.

explain: 원래 값보다 비싸게 몰래 되파는 표를 말해요. 이런 표를 파는 사람은 '암표상'이라고 불러요. '암표를 사다', '암표를 팔다', '암표 거래'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It means a ticket secretly resold at a price higher than the original. A person who sells such tickets is called a '암표상'. It is used in phrases like '암표를 사다', '암표를 팔다' and '암표 거래'.

examples.en: I pinned the paper to the bulletin board with a thumbtack.
It's dangerous to step on a tack that fell on the floor.
Please lend me a few thumbtacks.
I fixed the corners of the poster with thumbtacks.

examples.ko: 압정이 너무 짧아서 벽에 안 박혀요.
examples.en: The tack is too short, so it won't go into the wall.

examples.ko: 압정 상자를 쏟아서 한참 줍고 있어요.
examples.en: I spilled the box of tacks and have been picking them up for a while.

explain: 게시판이나 벽에 종이를 고정할 때 눌러 꽂는 작은 핀이에요. '압정을 꽂다', '압정을 박다', '압정으로 고정하다'처럼 써요. 끝이 뾰족해서 바닥에 떨어지면 위험하니까 조심해야 해요.
explain_en: It is a small pin you press in to fix paper to a bulletin board or wall. Typical patterns are '압정을 꽂다', '압정을 박다' and '압정으로 고정하다'. The point is sharp, so be careful when one falls on the floor.

examples.en: The front wheel of my bicycle went flat.
The front wheel was wobbling, so I went to the repair shop.
I replaced the motorcycle's front wheel with a new one.
The trick of riding with the front wheel up is difficult.
The car's front wheel fell into a puddle hole.
The front tire is badly worn.

explain: 앞쪽에 달린 바퀴이고 반대말은 '뒷바퀴'예요. 소리는 [압빠퀴]로 나니까 소리 나는 대로 쓰지 않도록 조심하세요. 자전거, 오토바이, 자동차 이야기에서 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is the wheel at the front, and the opposite is '뒷바퀴'. It is pronounced [압빠퀴], so be careful not to spell it as it sounds. It often comes up when talking about bicycles, motorcycles and cars.

examples.en: We climbed the mountain with the leader in front.
I put the child in front to find the way.

examples.ko: 경험 많은 선배를 앞장세워 행사를 준비했어요.
examples.en: We prepared the event with an experienced senior taking the lead.
Don't push others to the front; step up yourself.
If you have a guide go ahead, you won't get lost.
My friends made me go first.

explain: '앞장서다'는 스스로 앞에 서는 것이고, '앞장세우다'는 다른 사람을 앞에 서게 하는 거예요. 비슷한 말로 '앞세우다'가 있어요. 목적어 앞에 '을/를'을 붙여서 '누구를 앞장세우다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: '앞장서다' means to step forward on your own, while '앞장세우다' means to make someone else go in front. A similar word is '앞세우다'. It takes an object, as in '누구를 앞장세우다'.

examples.en: I am a longtime devoted reader of this magazine.
I would like to thank all our devoted readers.

examples.ko: 애독자 엽서를 보내면 선물을 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you send in a reader postcard, you can get a gift.

examples.ko: 그 작가의 애독자라서 신간을 바로 샀어요.
examples.en: I'm a devoted fan of that author, so I bought the new book right away.
As the novel became popular, its loyal readers increased.
Devoted readers sent many letters to the author.

explain: 책, 신문, 잡지를 좋아해서 꾸준히 읽는 사람을 말해서, 그냥 '독자'보다 애정이 느껴져요. 신문이나 잡지에서 '애독자 여러분'이라고 인사하는 말이 자주 나와요. '그 작가의 애독자'처럼 특정 작가나 책에도 써요.
explain_en: It refers to someone who loves a book, newspaper or magazine and reads it regularly, so it feels warmer than plain '독자'. Newspapers and magazines often greet readers with '애독자 여러분'. It can also be used for a particular author or book, as in '그 작가의 애독자'.

en: suffer hardships; have a hard time

examples.en: I had a hard time finding the way.

examples.ko: 아이가 말을 안 들어서 요즘 애먹고 있어요.
examples.en: My child won't listen, so I'm having a hard time these days.

examples.ko: 컴퓨터가 고장 나서 한참 동안 애먹었던 적이 있어요.
examples.en: There was a time I struggled for ages because my computer broke.
Didn't you have a really hard time moving?
I'm struggling a lot while learning a new job.

examples.ko: 감기 때문에 며칠 애먹고 이제 괜찮아요.
examples.en: I suffered with a cold for a few days, but I'm fine now.

explain: 일이 뜻대로 안 돼서 힘들거나 고생하는 상황에 써요. 보통 '-느라 애먹다', '-면서 애먹다'처럼 원인과 같이 말해요. 비슷한 '고생하다'보다 말하기에서 더 가볍게 써요. 노력한다는 뜻의 '애를 쓰다'와는 달라요.
explain_en: It is used when things don't go your way and you struggle or have a hard time. It is usually paired with the cause, as in '-느라 애먹다' or '-면서 애먹다'. It sounds lighter in speech than the similar '고생하다'. It is different from '애를 쓰다', which means to make an effort.

en: child who acts like an adult

examples.ko: 우리 아들은 애어른처럼 말해서 웃음이 나요.
examples.en: My son talks like a little adult, which makes me laugh.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때부터 애어른이라는 말을 자주 들었어요.
examples.en: Since I was little, I was often called an old soul.
My younger sibling acts like a little adult for his age.
She matured early and became like a little adult.
I'm proud of the child who acts so mature.

examples.ko: 부모님을 도우려고 애어른이 된 딸이 안쓰러워요.
examples.en: I feel sorry for my daughter, who grew up too fast to help her parents.

explain: 나이는 어리지만 말이나 행동이 어른 같은 아이를 말해요. '어른스럽다'와 비슷하지만 '애어른'은 아이가 너무 일찍 어른이 된 것 같아 안쓰러운 느낌이 들 때도 있어요. 칭찬일 수도, 걱정하는 말일 수도 있어서 상황을 보고 판단해야 해요.
explain_en: It describes a child who speaks or acts like an adult. It is similar to '어른스럽다', but '애어른' can also carry a feeling of pity, as if the child grew up too early. It can be praise or concern, so judge from the situation.

examples.en: I adopted a pet cat.
This animal is easy to keep as a pet.
I went to the mart to buy pet food.
A pet turtle definitely needs a tank.
I bought a toy at the pet supplies store.

examples.ko: 애완용 물고기 먹이를 하루에 한 번 줘요.
examples.en: I feed my pet fish once a day.

explain: '애완용 고양이', '애완용으로 키우다'처럼 뒤에 명사가 오거나 '으로'가 붙어 써요. 요즘은 가족으로 생각하는 마음을 담아 '반려동물', '반려견'이라는 말도 많이 써요. 사람이 아닌 동물에 대해 말하고 물건을 소개할 때는 '애완용품'이라는 말도 써요.
explain_en: It is used before a noun or with '으로', as in '애완용 고양이' and '애완용으로 키우다'. These days people also often say '반려동물' or '반려견' to show they think of the animal as family. For products you also see the word '애완용품' (pet supplies).
